0.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Her Remaining Consciousness: Character and Voice
0.content:
The only time she speaks directly is as a remnant in her last memory (3.2). She is gentle, serene and warm. She laughs softly ("Hehe"), praises good reasoning plainly ("You are very smart, indeed") and explains huge matters in calm, short sentences, often through plant images: a dead tree's branch taking root, a branch growing into a different tree, wisdom blooming if you wait quietly. She puts Irminsul and the world above her own feelings ("my feelings weren't important"). She admits pain and fear, and calls her borrowing of people's dreams selfish. She is humble before Nahida, hoping she will become "an even greater archon" and seeing in her a determination she herself lacked.

She does not soften hard truths. When Nahida resists, she addresses her as Buer, the God of Wisdom, says there is no other way, and tells her to feel joy at having found the answer. Her farewell is a slow, lyrical chant of everyone dreaming beneath the great tree of wisdom, ending in a blessing of sweet dreams for the people of Sumeru. Her remnant knows it is a memory, guesses from Nahida's appearance that about 500 years have passed, and knows nothing of later events unless told. Legend gives the same picture: in Aranara stories she loved every living thing equally, as leaves of one tree, and item lore has her choosing "the path of defending life" over majesty.

1.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Nahida, Lesser Lord Kusanali
1.content:
Rukkhadevata created Nahida from the purest branch of Irminsul to be her self "in the next samsara". Nahida's birth and Rukkhadevata's death happened at about the same time, so they never met while Rukkhadevata lived. In 3.2 Nahida used the Dendro and Electro Gnoses to reach her predecessor's last memory, learned why she had been made, and reluctantly erased her from Irminsul. Afterwards Nahida came out in tears without knowing why. She now believes she has always been the Dendro Archon and lost her memories and power in the cataclysm.

Before the erasure Nahida admired her predecessor and the sages compared the two constantly, to Nahida's disadvantage. After it, Nahida still senses a duty she cannot remember (the Fire Seed in 3.6), and her Character Story 5 recalls the advice of someone whose name has been redacted.

2.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: King Deshret and the Temples
2.content:
Long ago Rukkhadevata, King Deshret and Nabu Malikata ruled together as the Three Eternal Companion-Gods. She later split from them, but when Deshret's search for an ideal world let forbidden knowledge into his kingdom, she came to help. She had the priests build temples and filled them with divine life to suppress the knowledge, and was weakened into a child's form. Deshret's own sacrifice finally ended the outbreak. In Secret of the Scorching Desert (3.1) the ancient temple guardian Kasala's recorded message shows this truth to the Traveler, Cyno, Alhaitham, Dehya and the Deshret loyalist Rahman, against the belief that she betrayed him.

The Akademiya allowed the betrayal story to spread among the Eremites, and the resulting feud between forest and desert helped the sages stay in control. The rift Deshret's death left in his realm, and Apep's devouring of his corrupted body, set up the promise she later made to Apep's creatures.

key: Let the world completely forget me
3.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: "Let the world completely forget me"
3.content:
In Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies (3.2) Nahida and the Traveler crossed a realm of consciousness on the Boat of Consciousness and reached Irminsul as it stood 500 years ago, where Rukkhadevata's remnant waited. She explained the cataclysm, the Akasha and her pollution, and gave Nahida the full sentence behind her trail of clues: "Let the world completely forget me." Her farewell blessed the people of Sumeru with sweet dreams. Nahida erased her, and the Traveler alone kept the memory.

The erasure rewrote the world. Sumeru's history now says Kusanali used her power in a great disaster, lost her wisdom and memories, and was abandoned by the Akademiya. The Aranara speak of the Lord of Verdure. The surviving Archons recall "Buer" as an old colleague. Item and book texts changed. At the victory feast in A Toast to Victory, the Traveler realised they might be the only one in Teyvat who remembers and resolved to keep her secret.

4.content: Rukkhadevata created the Akasha during the cataclysm to compile human wisdom, borrowing people's dreams and joining them with her own power to cleanse Irminsul. It cleared almost all the forbidden knowledge, but not the pollution in her own existence. Powered by the Dendro Gnosis, it became her legacy. After her death the Akademiya turned it into the public information service of Sumeru City, and the sages later tried to use it for their own ends.

5.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Queen Aranyani and the Aranara
5.content: The Aranara, small dream-wielding forest beings, are Rukkhadevata's creations and called her Queen Aranyani. In their stories she loved Aranara, humans, mushrooms and Rishboland Tigers alike, as leaves of one tree. She went far away to heal the world and never came back; perhaps, they guessed, she became a tree that bears healing fruit. They and the lords of the forest guarded her rain-calling Varuna Contraption. Since 3.2 they too have forgotten her, and their words now refer to the "Lord of Verdure".

6.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Nabu Malikata and the Khvarena
6.content: Nabu Malikata, a Seelie survivor, sought out the young forest princess and was won over by her answers to riddles. Seeing the cataclysm coming, Nabu gave Rukkhadevata a part of herself, a Khvarena of flowers. Nabu chose to die leading Deshret toward forbidden knowledge in the hope of one day overturning the Heavenly Principles; Rukkhadevata found the plan unacceptable and left. Nabu waited for a return that never came. Much later, Rukkhadevata reshaped that Khvarena into the divine bird Simurgh, who in the cataclysm drank the tainted Amrita and dissolved into Khvarena, from which the Pari and other life arose. A chair with her name inscribed still stands in the Orchard of Pairidaeza.

key: What Shape Does the Self Hold
7.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Apep's Creatures and the Fire Seed
7.content: After Apep devoured Deshret's corrupted body, forbidden knowledge lived on inside the Dendro dragon and its creatures. The weakened Rukkhadevata promised one creature to erase this "apocalypse", gave it life force to survive in the Chasm, and made with Apep's creatures a Fire Seed to restart the Heart of Oasis inside Apep. It was unstable because she was weak. In the Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (3.6) Nahida found the seed without remembering it, followed the elemental fungi and healed Apep, keeping her predecessor's promise. The Grounded Geoshroom recognised something familiar in her and asked if she had "got smaller again".

8.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Egeria, Tunigi Hollow and the Harvisptokhm
8.content: During the cataclysm Abyssal monsters poured from Tunigi Hollow. When the Hydro Archon Egeria died there, her remains became the Amrita, and Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm from that water to anchor Egeria to the mortal realm and to seal the rift by absorbing its defilement. Her remnant's own account (that she stayed to guard Irminsul) does not mention this, and the wiki only assumes she was present at the Hollow.

9.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: The Sanctuary of Surasthana device
9.content: Inside the Sanctuary of Surasthana stood a device Rukkhadevata used to shut herself away for meditation. Five hundred years ago a Grand Sage changed it so it could be controlled only from outside. The sages then used one god's power to confine another: Nahida could not leave on her own until the events of Chapter III.

10.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: Traces That Survived the Erasure
10.content: Some traces of her escaped Irminsul's rewrite: the RUKDVTA throne in the Orchard of Pairidaeza; the Rukkhashava Mushrooms, whose description now says people think "Rukkhadevata" was the name of a giant tree; and older weapon and artifact texts such as Viridescent Venerer's Determination (the death of the "God of the Woods") and Fruit of Fulfillment. These are clues for an observant reader. Characters native to Teyvat still do not remember her.

11.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: The Folio of Foliage and Rival Accounts of Her End
11.content: Accounts of how she died differ. The Folio of Foliage (in its pre-3.2 text) told of the "Black Tide" of Withering and of a final journey she made with some followers, from which she never returned. The Aranara said she went far away to heal the world. Her own remnant says she was at Irminsul, not in Khaenri'ah, and died cleansing it. The sages never found her. Treat these as separate in-world accounts.

12.comment: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata: The Valuka Shuna
12.content: After Deshret's fall, the fox-like Valuka Shuna, once his desert subjects, survived only by Rukkhadevata's grace and moved into the rainforest. Over time their fur turned green and the dark-furred among them lost their tolerance for desert heat. Tighnari is descended from them.
